item.title: SA gives green light for gas to help power future data centres
item.description: The South Australian government says it is "absolutely fine" for gas to be used to help power data centres, despite its strategy focusing on renewable energy as the source.
item.dc:creator: James Wakelin

media:group.media:description: The proposed data centre at Bundey in SA's Mid North would require up to 800 megawatts of electricity to operate.

item.title: Only four government ministers have saved money this year. Here's who
item.description: As the government pursues savings "across the board" ahead of the mid-year budget update, an ABC analysis shows only a handful of ministers have managed net savings so far this year.
item.dc:creator: Tom Crowley

media:group.media:description: Jim Chalmers and Katy Gallagher have flagged further savings in the mid-year budget update.

item.title: Financial pain of outer suburbs fuelled demise of David Jones, experts say
item.description: After 188 years, David Jones announced it would close 19 stores, most of them in Sydney's outer suburbs.
item.dc:creator: Sean Tarek Goodwin

media:group.media:description: Economic pain felt in outer suburban areas could have fast-tracked the problems that overtook David Jones.

item.title: Salmon deaths at 'eye-watering' levels in Macquarie Harbour
item.description: Almost 2,000 tonnes of farmed salmon died over a 15-month period in Macquarie Harbour on Tasmania’s west coast, new data shows.
item.dc:creator: Jano Gibson

media:group.media:description: The EPA regulates 10 salmon leases in the harbour.

item.title: Bowen pushes pragmatic climate deal amid pressure over fossil fuels
item.description: Chris Bowen says Australia's coal and gas exports have not damaged its standing in climate negotiations, as countries struggle to agree on how to move away from fossil fuels.

media:group.media:description: Chris Bowen rejects suggestions Australia's role as a major fossil fuel exporter has damaged its standing in the negotiations.

item.title: Lifesaving medicines frequently in short supply and doctors are worried
item.description: ABC analysis reveals the important medicines that are repeatedly hard to source, highlighting supply chain weaknesses that could get worse.
item.dc:creator: Madi Chwasta, Jarrod Fankhauser, Joshua Byrd, and Cristen Tilley

item.title: Data centre industry butts up against community challenges
item.description: The peak body for the data centre industry says community consultation remains a sticking point, as Quantum DC halts its Tungkillo project.
item.dc:creator: Evelyn Leckie and Thomas Kelsall

media:group.media:description: Data centre companies are reportedly grappling with how to get community engagement "right".

item.title: Nvidia without succession plan as CEO Jensen Huang resigns
item.description: Jensen Huang, the co-founder, president and chief executive, has resigned, leaving the tech giant in a precarious position with no clear next leader.
item.dc:creator: Annabel Bowles

media:group.media:description: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia could leave a leadership vacuum at the leading AI chip company.

item.title: Coalmine reopens despite previous owners saying royalties made it unprofitable
item.description: A new Queensland company has purchased its fourth Bowen Basin coal mine, employing 275 workers to reopen a coalmine.
item.dc:creator: Liam O'Connell

media:group.media:description: Dump trucks on the haul road at the mine.

item.title: Hunt is on for heir to strange block of land
item.description: Could you be the long-lost owner of a 16m by 60cm strip of land in south-east Queensland, whose last known owner was August Thorsborne, a 19th-century businessman who died more than 100 years ago? The Department of Transport and Main Roads needs to know.
item.dc:creator: Ellen-Maree Elliot

media:group.media:description: Des Crump is a historian and bottle collector who has researched August Thorsborne.

item.title: Commercial rock lobster fisheries closed due to antibiotic trade risk
item.description: Commercial rock lobster and dive fisheries in parts of Tasmania's south-east will be closed for three months to "mitigate trade risks" linked to antibiotic use by the salmon industry.
item.dc:creator: Jano Gibson

media:group.media:description: The fisheries in parts of Tasmania's south-east will be closed to mitigate trade risks.

item.title: ANZ boss warns global markets in 'dangerous situation' as interest rates rise
item.description: ANZ boss Nuno Matos says he sees a "dangerous situation" of rising rates and frothy equity markets.
item.dc:creator: Gareth Hutchens

media:group.media:description: Nuno Matos says governments should be careful about competing too aggressively for global capital.

item.title: 'If they're winning, we're winning': Suppliers on David Jones closures
item.description: Some suppliers think a streamlined David Jones could be good news for their sales if it encourages more shoppers into fewer, higher-performing stores.
item.dc:creator: Liana Walker

media:group.media:description: David Jones has announced plans to close half its stores.

item.title: Train passengers stranded for hours with no aircon, no food and full toilets
item.description: Buses have been called in to get passengers home as track repair work continues.
item.dc:creator: Grace Whiteside, Russell Varley, and James C Taylor

media:group.media:description: Fire crews were called to help stranded passengers.

item.title: 'I had to have it': Boag's worker wins auction for last Tasmanian brew
item.description: The final Tasmanian-brewed Boag's Red case is sold at auction for $1,300 to a brewery electrician who says it's going straight on display in his lounge room.
item.dc:creator: Bec Pridham

media:group.media:description: Sam Cox with the last carton of Launceston-brewed Boag's Red.

item.title: How India is marketing its skilled workforce to Australian businesses
item.description: India has positioned itself as a global hub of skilled, cheap labour, and Australian companies are cashing in and moving more jobs to its shores.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Clayton

media:group.media:description: Qantas is cutting 850 local jobs with some roles to be outsourced to Accenture workers in India.

item.title: Personal data stolen after National Parks booking service hacked in three states
item.description: The National Parks booking system for Queensland, Victoria and South Australia has suffered a data breach, with hackers stealing personal user information.
item.dc:creator: Kenji Sato

media:group.media:description: Park users are being warned to keep an eye out for Queensland Parks and Wildlife staff impersonators.

item.title: Police uncover organised thefts during country shoplifting blitz
item.description: Police say there is evidence of organisation behind retail theft in Shepparton, where an operation targeting repeat offenders has led to more than 200 arrests.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Perez

media:group.media:description: In May, police launched Operation Securus, focusing on retail theft in Shepparton's shopping district.

item.title: Superhuman AI bots will not steal this man's job
item.description: Luke Gnocco remains pretty relaxed about artificial intelligence because, as he points out, "electronics and water usually don't work".
item.dc:creator: Isabella Garrido

media:group.media:description: Luke Gnocco is the founder of Poseidon Adventure, which operates out of Townsville and Brisbane.

item.title: Developer says gigantic WA data centre will not use fracked gas
item.description: Concerns about the proposed mega data centre in Western Australia come amid growing opposition to similar facilities in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Jess Baker

media:group.media:description: Gingerah Energy's proposed data centre project includes a local micro-grid powered by a 5,200-megawatt solar farm and 250 wind turbines.

item.title: Commonwealth Bank allegedly overcharged business customers
item.description: Commonwealth Bank allegedly overcharged millions of dollars in fees to tens of thousands of business customers, many of them small businesses, according to the corporate regulator.
item.dc:creator: Nassim Khadem

media:group.media:description: The CBA faces allegations it failed to report cash transactions made through intelligent deposit machines.

item.title: Developer 'pauses' AI data centre proposal after it 'misread' community feeling
item.description: Quantum DC has delayed its proposed hyper-scale AI data centre in the Adelaide Hills after receiving more than 400 questions from the community.
item.dc:creator: Isabella Carbone

media:group.media:description: A community protest event held in Mannum against the Tungkillo data centre last month.

item.title: Nvidia board meets after Jensen Huang allegedly had second affair
item.description: Numerous reports say the Nvidia board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he allegedly had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Adelaide Miller and David Taylor

media:group.media:description: NVIDIA founder Jensen Huang has stepped down from his role as the company's CEO.

item.title: Labor pledges to boost regional rail and attacks Liberal costings
item.description: Labor is promising a $420 million boost to Victoria's regional rail services while attacking the Liberal leader's commitment to each a cash surplus by 2032.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Eddie

media:group.media:description: Labor is promising to increase the number of regional train services if elected.

item.title: Rising costs hurt South Australia's regional high streets
item.description: Several shops in Mount Gambier's economic heart stand empty as rising costs and changing shopping habits take a toll.
item.dc:creator: Sam Bradbrook

media:group.media:description: Mount Gambier's Commercial Street in 1964, from the Life in Australia film series.
